rule_summary: Adopters must be older than 25 (mayor de veinticinco años). For a couple, it is enough that one partner is.
notes: Catalonia applies its own civil code (see the CT rows).

rule_summary: The age gap between adopter and child must be at least 16 years and at most 45 years.
notes: For a couple, one adopter within 45 years is enough. The upper gap can be larger for sibling groups or children with special needs.

rule_summary: One person or a couple may adopt. Only spouses, or a couple in a similar stable relationship, can adopt a child together.
People who cannot be legal guardians (tutores) under the law cannot foster or adopt.
The public body must declare adopters suitable (declaración de idoneidad) first. This needs a psychosocial assessment of their personal, family and social situation.
notes: The assessment also looks at their ability to form secure bonds and their parenting skills.

rule_summary: People who offer to adopt must attend information and preparation sessions. The public body or an authorised partner organisation runs them.
notes: No hours are set in national law.

rule_summary: People who have lost or had suspended their parental authority cannot be declared suitable. Nor can people whose own child is in public care.
Foster care can be with the child's relatives (familia extensa) or with another family (familia ajena). Care with another family can be specialised.
Foster care is emergency (mainly for children under 6, up to 6 months), temporary (up to 2 years) or permanent.
notes: Temporary care can be extended in the child's interest. Permanent carers can ask a judge for some guardianship powers.

rule_summary: Specialised foster care needs a family member with relevant qualifications, experience or training. If it is full-time (dedicación exclusiva), the carers receive compensation.
legal_citation: Ley Orgánica 1/1996 de Protección Jurídica del Menor, art. 20.1
notes: Some communities also have professional foster care (acogimiento profesionalizado), where carers are employed by the public body.

rule_summary: Before a placement, the public body assesses the family. It looks at family situation, parenting ability, motivation and willingness to support contact with the birth family.
National law sets no upper age for foster carers. Where the type of care calls for it, the public body considers whether the carers' age suits the child's.
Relatives (familia extensa) who meet the conditions get priority, unless the child's interest points elsewhere.
Foster carers have a right to information, preparation before placement, follow-up and specialist support during and after the placement.
Foster carers have a right to any financial compensation and other help that has been agreed. National law sets no amount.
notes: Each community sets its own amounts (see the community rows).

rule_summary: Work or activities with regular contact with children need a clean certificate from the Central Register of Sex Offenders (Registro Central de Delincuentes Sexuales).
legal_citation: Ley Orgánica 8/2021 de protección integral a la infancia y la adolescencia frente a la violencia (LOPIVI), art. 57.1
notes: The article speaks of professions and activities. Madrid, Catalonia, Valencia and Castilla-La Mancha ask foster applicants for this certificate.

rule_summary: For international adoption, the suitability declaration and its reports are valid for up to 3 years, if the family's situation does not change.
Employees who adopt, take guardianship for adoption or foster get 19 weeks' paid leave each. A single carer gets 32 weeks.
notes: Changed by Royal Decree-law 9/2025. Article 45.1.d sets which foster placements qualify.

rule_summary: Public payments for fostering children are exempt from personal income tax.
legal_citation: Ley 35/2006 del Impuesto sobre la Renta de las Personas Físicas, art. 7.i

rule_summary: Family care comes before residential care, especially for children under 6. Children under 3 should not go into residential care unless family care is impossible.
notes: Where it does happen, residential care for these children should not, as a rule, last more than 3 months.

rule_summary: Information sessions are compulsory before an offer to foster. They last about 2 hours and are booked at the provincial office.
notes: Law 4/2021, art. 100.2, also makes them compulsory.

rule_summary: Training sessions must take place within 3 months of the offer. The public body then gives the family a certificate.
legal_citation: Ley 4/2021 de Infancia y Adolescencia de Andalucía, art. 100.3

rule_summary: Information sessions are compulsory before an offer to adopt. Preparation sessions take place within 3 months of the offer.
The public body must issue its decision on suitability to foster within 3 months.
notes: The assessment starts after the family has finished training.

rule_summary: The public body must decide on suitability to adopt within 3 months. Without a decision in that time, the offer counts as refused.
No fixed upper age. The assessment checks that the carers' age lets them meet the child's needs until at least age 18.
A suitability declaration for fostering lasts 3 years and must then be updated.
notes: Families must report changes in their situation at any time.

rule_summary: After a finding of unsuitability, people must wait at least 1 year before making a new offer.
Relatives (familia extensa) always get preference when the provincial office selects a family. Relatives can start with their own offer form.
An offer must give an age range of at least 3 years for one child. The range is at least 4 years for 2 siblings and 5 for 3 or more.
notes: Offers that discriminate by sex, ethnicity or family background are not accepted.

rule_summary: The basic payment is €398.66 a month for each child.
notes: The page does not say when these rates took effect.

rule_summary: Temporary foster care with an unrelated family (familia ajena) pays €553.71 a month for each child.
notes: The page does not say when these rates took effect.

rule_summary: Emergency and specialised foster care pay an extra €708.73 a month on top of the basic payment.
notes: The page does not say when these rates took effect. One-off help can also cover costs such as orthodontics or physiotherapy.

rule_summary: Foster payments do not count as household income for other help from the Junta de Andalucía.
Applicants to foster a child they do not know must be over 25. For a couple, one partner is enough.
An information session at the provincial office is compulsory before applying. Suitability is assessed after a training course.
notes: The training uses practical group work and self-reflection (IASS page).

rule_summary: An application to foster cannot run at the same time as an application for national adoption.
Each applicant gives a medical report on their physical and mental health, using the official model.
The application includes a check that applicants have no criminal record.
notes: The page lists a criminal record check among the documents. It does not say who in the household is checked.

rule_summary: Temporary and permanent foster care pays a basic €11.66 a day for each child.
notes: Order published in the Aragon gazette on 9 June 2017. Read on a legal publisher's copy. Amounts may have changed since.

rule_summary: Emergency foster care pays a basic €23.32 a day for each child, with at least 10 days paid per placement.
notes: Read on a legal publisher's copy of the 2017 order.

rule_summary: Families approved for emergency care receive €6 a day for being available when no child is placed.
notes: The order gives a cap of 1,200 days a year, as written. Supplements apply for disability and travel.

rule_summary: Aragon lists emergency, temporary, permanent, specialised and professional foster care. Professional carers have an employment contract with the public body.
notes: It also lists 'referential' care (acogimiento referencial), which gives children in residential homes time with a family.

rule_summary: The provincial office follows up each placement at least every 6 months.
Information sessions are compulsory before applying to foster. Relatives and people already close to the child are exempt.
legal_citation: Ley 8/2026 de Infancia y Adolescencia del Principado de Asturias, art. 85
notes: Law of 15 October 2026. It takes effect 1 month after publication in the Asturias gazette.

rule_summary: Training is compulsory before the assessment. It must be offered within 3 months of the application.
notes: Law of 15 October 2026. It takes effect 1 month after publication in the Asturias gazette.

rule_summary: The public body has 6 months from the application to decide on suitability. Without a decision, the application counts as refused.
notes: Law of 15 October 2026. It takes effect 1 month after publication in the Asturias gazette.

rule_summary: Suitability to foster is reviewed every 3 years.
notes: Law of 15 October 2026. It takes effect 1 month after publication in the Asturias gazette.

rule_summary: Foster carers receive a payment that reflects their availability and how demanding the placement is. Amounts are set by regulation.
notes: Payments do not count as household income for other Asturias help. Law of 15 October 2026. It takes effect 1 month after publication in the Asturias gazette.

rule_summary: Information sessions are compulsory before an offer to adopt. Training must take place within 3 months of the application.
notes: Law of 15 October 2026. It takes effect 1 month after publication in the Asturias gazette.

rule_summary: The decision on suitability to adopt is due within 3 months of the application. It is valid for 3 years.
notes: Without a decision in that time, the request counts as refused. Law of 15 October 2026. It takes effect 1 month after publication in the Asturias gazette.

rule_summary: The island councils (Consells Insulars) hold the powers on guardianship, foster care and adoption on each island.
legal_citation: Ley 8/1997, de atribución de competencias a los consejos insulares en materia de tutela, acogimiento y adopción de menores

rule_summary: In Menorca, foster care of one child pays €467.14 a month in 2026.
legal_citation: Acord del Consell Executiu del Consell Insular de Menorca, 26 January 2026 (BOIB 17, 5 February 2026)
notes: Menorca only: each island council sets its own rates. Amounts for 2026, raised 2.9% in line with prices.

rule_summary: In Menorca, foster care of 2 or more children pays €418.48 a month for each child in 2026.
legal_citation: Acord del Consell Executiu del Consell Insular de Menorca, 26 January 2026 (BOIB 17, 5 February 2026)
notes: Menorca only: each island council sets its own rates. Amounts for 2026, raised 2.9% in line with prices.

rule_summary: In Menorca, emergency and specialised foster care pay €1,000.13 a month for each child in 2026.
legal_citation: Acord del Consell Executiu del Consell Insular de Menorca, 26 January 2026 (BOIB 17, 5 February 2026)
notes: Menorca only: each island council sets its own rates. Amounts for 2026, raised 2.9% in line with prices.

rule_summary: In Menorca, applicants take a specific 10-hour training course as well as the assessment.
notes: Menorca only. Weekend and holiday families also take a 10-hour course.

rule_summary: Couples who offer to adopt must have lived together for at least the 2 years before the offer.
legal_citation: Ley 2/2024 de Infancia y Adolescencia, art. 259.c

rule_summary: Adopters need stable and sufficient means of living.
Adopters need physical and mental health that allows normal care of the child.
For sibling groups or children with special needs, the adopters' age must not be likely to limit the child's development.
Suitability to adopt needs information and preparation sessions run by the provincial councils (Diputaciones Forales).
The provincial council must offer training before a placement starts, and support during and after it. It may also offer financial help.
notes: The law leaves the suitability requirements for foster carers to regulations (art. 228.3).

rule_summary: In Gipuzkoa, specialised foster carers need specific training and at least 2 years' practical experience.
notes: From a 2020 campaign dossier of the Diputación Foral de Gipuzkoa. Gipuzkoa only.

rule_summary: The public body decides on the suitability of relatives who offer to foster within 6 months.
notes: This e-office procedure is for relatives (familia extensa).

rule_summary: Adopters must live in the Canary Islands.
legal_citation: Ley 1/1997 de Atención Integral a los Menores, art. 73.1

rule_summary: In simple and permanent foster care, health, education and living costs may be paid where essential. Amounts are set by regulation.
notes: The 1997 law uses the older term 'simple' foster care.

rule_summary: The law provides for professional foster care. Regulations set the most children per home and the payment.
Foster carers of a child in the community's care can receive a payment from the public social services system.
legal_citation: Ley 8/2010 de garantía de derechos y atención a la infancia y la adolescencia, art. 83
notes: No amount was found; the Cantabria e-office did not load in this session.

rule_summary: People fostering for the first time a child they have no close bond with must receive specific training first.
legal_citation: Ley 14/2002 de Promoción, Atención y Protección a la Infancia en Castilla y León, art. 93.4

rule_summary: Where the aim is not adoption, relatives or people with a previous good relationship with the child get preference.
The assessment of adopters looks at housing, any couple relationship and a shared wish to adopt. It also checks willingness to tell the child about the adoption.
The assessment of people offering to adopt lasts at most 6 months.
At least one applicant must be over 25. This does not apply to relatives.
legal_citation: Ley 7/2023 de Atención y Protección a la Infancia y la Adolescencia de Castilla-La Mancha, art. 64.2.a
notes: The regional foster page also says any adult or family over 25 may apply.

rule_summary: Everyone in the household needs no record of family violence, crimes against children or sexual crimes. A clean sex offenders register certificate shows this.
The public body sets compulsory training for foster carers. It covers the assessment, the waiting time and the placement.
notes: No hours are set in the law.

rule_summary: An interdisciplinary team assesses families through interviews and training sessions. Approved families join the regional register of foster families.
notes: Law 7/2023, art. 67, lists the assessment criteria, including age and health.

rule_summary: A suitability declaration to adopt expires after 3 years. A renewal is decided within 3 months.
notes: Families who renew within 2 months of expiry keep their place in the order.

rule_summary: Adopters must be over 25. For a couple, one partner is enough.
legal_citation: Codi civil de Catalunya, llibre segon (Llei 25/2010), art. 235-30
notes: Exceptions apply for a spouse's or partner's child and for orphaned relatives.

rule_summary: Adopters must be at least 14 years older than the child. The Catalan civil code sets no upper age gap.
notes: The value is the minimum gap. National law (16 to 45 years) does not apply in Catalonia.

rule_summary: Only spouses or a stable couple (parella estable) can adopt together.
Applicants give a criminal record certificate and a clean certificate for sexual offences. With consent, the institute checks these itself.
notes: Page updated 16 July 2026.

rule_summary: Applicants give a medical report on physical and mental health. They must have no illness that prevents care of the child.
Applicants need sufficient means of living and suitable housing.
The assessment includes at least 3 individual interviews, one at home, and training sessions. A partner organisation (ICIF) writes a psychosocial report.
Simple and permanent foster care pays a basic €511 for a child aged 0 to 9.
notes: €548 for ages 10 to 14 and €580 for 15 to 18. A respite supplement of €90 or €120 is added. The table does not state the period; we read it as monthly.

rule_summary: Emergency and assessment foster care (urgència i diagnòstic) pays a basic €511 plus a €700 supplement.
notes: €1,211 is our total of the two amounts. The table does not state the period; we read it as monthly.

rule_summary: Care in an educational living unit (UCAE) adds a €1,800 supplement to the basic payment for each child's age.
notes: A €545 disability supplement and supplements for 3 to 5 children may also apply. The table does not state the period; we read it as monthly.

rule_summary: Catalonia has emergency and assessment, simple, permanent and UCAE foster care. In UCAE care, a family member has a relevant qualification, training and experience.
notes: Simple foster care aims for the child to go home within 2 years.

rule_summary: Weekend and holiday care by a collaborating family is for children aged about 9 and over in residential homes. It brings no payment.
Foster care is not a step towards adoption. A family cannot foster while it waits to adopt.
Applicants must be adults with full legal capacity.
notes: Decree 9/2014 governs the procedure.

rule_summary: Applicants to foster a child they do not know must live in Extremadura.
People found unsuitable to foster or adopt in the last 24 months cannot apply to foster a child they do not know.
Couples apply together. Unmarried couples must be in the regional register of couples (Registro de Parejas de Hecho).
Applicants must have no record of homicide, injury, sexual offences or family crimes against relatives or children. Other adults at home also give certificates.
Before the assessment, families take specific training of at least 3 sessions in person. Employees may take time off work for it.
From 1 May 2025, families fostering a child aged 1 to 18 receive €425 a month.
notes: Xunta press release of 30 April 2025. The Xunta says it raised these payments twice in 4 years (press release of 9 July 2026).

rule_summary: Families fostering a child under 1 receive €600 a month.
notes: Xunta press release of 30 April 2025.

rule_summary: Galicia runs a pilot of specialised, full-time foster care (dedicación exclusiva).
notes: Press release of 9 July 2026. The Xunta plans over €3 million for it until mid-2029.

rule_summary: Applicants must be over 25 and live in the Comunidad de Madrid.
notes: The e-office page says this applies to married couples, couples and single people.

rule_summary: Applicants must live in the Comunidad de Madrid. Relatives and people with a close previous bond with the child are exempt.
legal_citation: Ley 4/2023 de Derechos, Garantías y Protección Integral de la Infancia y la Adolescencia de la Comunidad de Madrid, art. 96.1.d

rule_summary: For couples, the assessment looks for at least 3 years of living together.
notes: Listed among the criteria for assessing offers.

rule_summary: Applicants give a criminal record certificate and a clean certificate from the sex offenders register.
notes: Law 4/2023, art. 96.1.a, also bars people convicted of sexual or trafficking offences.

rule_summary: Applicants give medical certificates showing no illness that prevents caring for a child like the one they offer for.
Applicants show regular household income, usually with their latest tax return. The law asks for stable and sufficient means.
An information session, in person or online, is required before the formal application. The psychosocial study includes a training course.
Relatives who know of the protection measure have up to 3 months from the decision to offer to foster.
Since 1 January 2026, general foster care pays €500 a month for each child.
notes: Regional press release of 30 June 2026. Decree 44/2022 set €300 in 2022. A September 2026 announcement plans €600 from 2027.

rule_summary: Foster care of a child with special difficulties, such as disability or complex medical needs, pays €1,000 a month.
notes: Press release of 30 June 2026. The September 2026 announcement plans €1,200 from 2027.

rule_summary: Emergency foster families, who care for children up to age 6, receive €2,000 a month.
notes: Press release of 30 June 2026. Decree 44/2022 set €1,200 a month for each family in 2022. €2,500 is planned from 2027.

rule_summary: Since 2026, families who take in a young person over 12 receive an extra €1,000 a month.
notes: Press release of 30 June 2026.

rule_summary: AcogES+ is full-time specialised foster care run with Aldeas Infantiles SOS. The carer has a contract with the organisation.
notes: A separate specialised pilot is run with Redes AFE.

rule_summary: A suitability declaration to adopt is valid for up to 3 years, if the family's situation does not change.
Where no specific family is indicated, offers with an age gap of 40 years or less get preference. For couples, their average age counts.
Where no specific family is indicated, offers from couples get preference over offers from single people.
Any adult, couple or family may foster.
notes: Manual published in May 2026 by Cruz Roja Española with the Region of Murcia.

rule_summary: All members of the household must accept and agree to the placement.
Applicants need good health, family and emotional stability, and stable means of living.
The decision on suitability to foster is due within 6 months of the offer.
legal_citation: Ley Foral 12/2022 de atención y protección a niños, niñas y adolescentes y de promoción de sus familias, derechos e igualdad, art. 126

rule_summary: Suitability to foster is reassessed after 3 years.
Applicants must not be expecting a baby, awaiting an adoption, or in fertility treatment. After a birth or adoption they wait at least 6 months.
The decision on suitability to adopt is due within 7 months of a complete application. It is valid for up to 3 years.
Adopters need a certificate showing no criminal record. They must also live in Navarre and complete training first.
Specialised foster carers commit to training, follow-up reports and, as a rule, full-time care by the trained carer.
notes: Undated leaflet on navarra.es. It cites Decreto Foral 7/2009.

rule_summary: The assessment of suitability to adopt must not take more than 6 months from the application.
legal_citation: Ley 1/2006 de protección de menores de La Rioja, art. 98.1

rule_summary: A suitability declaration expires after 3 years unless circumstances change. A renewal is decided within 3 months.
The law provides for professional foster care. Regulations set the most children, the payment and the training.
An emergency placement made while an urgent protection decision is confirmed cannot last more than 3 months.
Any adult living in the Valencian Community may offer to foster.
legal_citation: Decreto 35/2021 de regulación del acogimiento familiar, art. 24.1

rule_summary: Applicants must live in the Valencian Community.
Applicants must show a clean certificate from the Central Register of Sex Offenders.
legal_citation: Ley 26/2018 de derechos y garantías de la infancia y la adolescencia, art. 130.2

rule_summary: The decision on suitability to foster is due within 6 months of starting the procedure. Without it, the offer counts as refused.
Emergency families (familias de atención inmediata) can offer to take up to 2 children at once. Larger sibling groups need a prior assessment.
Emergency families must be available 24 hours a day, all year. They can ask for 22 working days' rest a year without losing pay.
The foster payment does not count as household income for other public help, and it cannot be seized.
notes: No amount found. Decree 64/2026 changed the payment article of Decree 35/2021 (seen in web search results only).

rule_summary: Suitability to adopt is valid for 3 years and is reviewed every year.
